::: post-intro
Citi Bike Trip #495.

- **Depart:** Broadway and W 39th St., 9:18am
- **Arrive:** Washington Pl. and Broadway, 9:33am
- **Trip time:** 14:52 minutes
:::

One of the snarls on this path from midtown to NYU is Herald Square. It's at the intersection of 34th Street, Broadway, and 6th Ave. Sixth Ave is one-way uptown. Broadway is one-way downtown, and cuts diagonally across the north-south avenues. Usually the lanes go in the same direction as traffic. But as Broadway cuts across 6th, the downtown bike lane runs along the west side of 6th, against traffic, for a half a block.

Bikers will often complain about erratic, do-whatever-they-want pedestrians. My colleague Drew points out that all NYC folks, no matter their mode of transportation (car, foot, bike), will blame the others for whatever traffic problems they encounter. But here in Herald square it is largely ignored by pedestrians that the green zones are for bikes.

I usually combat this by keeping my thumb on the bell and ringing it frequently, to let pedestrians know I have the right of way and intend on taking it. Today I encountered a fellow Citi Biker with a different tactic. As he rode through the lane he shouted repeatedly:

> The promise of a green America is ruined when people walk in the bike lane!

At the next light we chatted, and he told me he found it more satisfying than simply shouting “Get out of the bike lane!” I don't know if it's more effective.
